newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Daewoo mulls bid for Bulgaria GSM conTract.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo mulls bid for Bulgaria GSM conTract.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Corp said on Thursday it would bid for a second GSM operator contract in Bulgaria if the government launched a tender.
"We are very much interested in participating in a tender for a second GSM operator in Bulgaria," Chung-Hwan Kim, representative of Daewoo's Sofia branch office, told a news conference.
Kim said the company was also interested in Bulgaria's plans for a partial sale of its state-owned telecommunication company BTC.
The government has approved the sale of up to 25 percent of BTC, the country's telecommunications monopoly.
"We are interested in principle in buying the BTC stake," Kim said.
Telecom officials say the price of the BTC stake would be higher if the company participated in a venture as a GSM operator.
Post and Communication Committee chief Lyubomir Kolarov said recently the committee had already prepared the conditions for two GSM tenders and one of them would be compulsory for a BTC partner.
He did not specify when BTC planned to launch the tenders for a GSM operator.
Bulgaria's only GSM operator Mobiltel recently postponed its shareholders' meeting until it completed talks with potential buyers.
Mobiltel is a joint venture set up by one of Bulgaria's major private financial groups Tron and was granted the country's first GSM licence two years ago.

The venture's GSM, which started operating last September, covers parts of Sofia, Bulgaria's other main cities of Plovdiv and Varna, and three more towns. It has contracts for roaming with 12 GSM operators in 11 countries. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
